races.name: Boodles Anniversary 4-Y-O Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Maestro Conti
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with excellent Grade 2 form and strong 14-day trainer record, ideally positioned for this race shape
runners_data.comment: Travelled smoothly for a long way when runner-up in the Triumph last month; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Untroubled to win sole start in France and scored in good style at Kempton (2m, good) and Cheltenham (Grade 2) in first two runs for Dan Skelton; well backed into 5-1 when runner-up in the Triumph Hurdle at Cheltenham (2m1f, soft) last month, when he travelled smoothly for a long way before keeping on well to edge out Minella Study in the battle for second; has leading claims on that form and he should be unfazed by this return to a sharper track.

runners_data.name: Mange Tout
runners_data.note: Half-sister to Grade 1 winner with solid prominent style but 66 days off concerns after heavy ground defeat
runners_data.comment: Third in Grade 1 at Leopardstown but was behind Selma De Vary and needs to resume progress
runners_data.spotlight: Half-sister to multiple Grade 1 winner Impaire Et Passe; won her first three starts over hurdles before a third in Grade 1 at Leopardstown (2m, heavy) in February; may have more to offer in this sphere but she finished behind Selma De Vary last time and needs to resume progress.

runners_data.name: Selma De Vary
runners_data.note: French import for Mullins with prominent style, though heavy ground form mixed and 4th last time suggests vulnerability
runners_data.comment: Got hampered in closing stages when fourth in the Triumph; big player for Willie Mullins
runners_data.spotlight: Ran twice on Flat in France and three times in hurdle races at Auteuil, culminating in a win in November (2m1f, heavy); made a promising start for new yard when runner-up behind Narciso Has in a Grade 1 at Leopardstown in February; didn't come from so far back when fourth in the Triumph at Cheltenham last month but she made smooth progress and kept on well after being hampered in the closing stages; that makes her one of the form picks in this field and Willie Mullins has won this twice in the last three years.

runners_data.name: Indian River
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs pace collapse, exposed when stepped up in class at Grade level
runners_data.comment: Triple hurdle winner but his limitations were exposed in the Triumph (tenth) last month
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in his two Irish Flat maidens; justified favouritism in first three starts over hurdles but his limitations were exposed when a never-dangerous tenth in the Triumph at Cheltenham (50-1) last month; passed over.

runners_data.name: Aqua Bleu
runners_data.note: Front-runner with perfect hurdles record but all wins came at lower grades, faces stronger pace pressure here
runners_data.comment: Front-runner who is 3-4 over hurdles but he has a lot to find in this Grade 1 contest
runners_data.spotlight: Promising second on debut at Hereford (2m, good) in November and he's unbeaten in three runs since; has looked a very willing front-runner but all his wins have been in small-field events and he has a lot to find in this Grade 1 contest.

runners_data.name: Winston Junior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner learning to settle better, decent recent form but trainer's 1/8 record notable
runners_data.comment: Second in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham and he's open to more progress; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Useful maiden on the Flat at up 1m5f and he has a record of 2212 since switched to hurdling for his current yard; seems to be learning to settle better and he didn't get a smooth run when an eye-catching second in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham (2m, good to soft) last month; that was another good step forward and he could continue to progress in this sphere; interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Wolf Rayet
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who ran well in Triumph at big price but beaten favourite last time suggests limitations
runners_data.comment: Ran well at a massive price in the Triumph but beaten 10l and he was behind three of these
runners_data.spotlight: Three Flat runs in Ireland and four over hurdles in Britain; ran well at a massive price in the Triumph at Cheltenham (eighth of 20) last month but he was beaten 10l and finished behind three of today's rivals; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Ammes
runners_data.note: Former good flat horse with prominent style, 30 days off and heavy ground form question marks
runners_data.comment: Listed runner-up but he was well held in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham last month
runners_data.spotlight: Good Flat horse who won his first two starts over hurdles before a close second behind Minella Study in a Listed race at Wetherby (2m, good) in October; still has potential in this sphere but he was only 12th in the juvenile handicap at Cheltenham last month and needs to resume his progress in this tough race; visor added.

runners_data.name: Lord
runners_data.note: Course winner and front-runner but 68 days absence and form tailed off after December peak
runners_data.comment: 4-7 over hurdles but this is a tough test and he has plenty to find on the figures
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 4-6 over hurdles when returning to form with an all-the-way win in a Listed event over C&D (soft) in December; ran to a similar level when runner-up in the Scottish Triumph at Musselburgh in January but this is a much tougher test and he has plenty to find on the figures; cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Minella Study
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong Triumph third, excellent recent form and proven at this level
runners_data.comment: Close third in the Triumph when he split Maestro Conti and Selma De Vary; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Six-race maiden on the Flat but he's 3-4 over hurdles and travelled strongly for a long way when close third in the Triumph at Cheltenham last month; split Maestro Conti and Selma De Vary in that race and should make another bold bid here; that last run was on soft but his second win was on good.

races.paceDynamic: Lord and Aqua Bleu will contest the early lead, both confirmed front-runners who should ensure an honest gallop from the start. The prominent brigade of Maestro Conti, Mange Tout, Selma De Vary, and Winston Junior creates significant mid-race congestion, particularly dangerous approaching the final two hurdles on soft ground. Hold-up horses Indian River and Wolf Rayet face a tactical disadvantage with limited room for manoeuvre behind a strong pace. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can avoid the early speed battle but stay close enough to strike when the leaders tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent brigade strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders Lord and Aqua Bleu set a strong pace but fade from 3 out
scenarios.body: The race falls to one of the prominent quartet who can track the pace without getting involved in the early speed battle. Maestro Conti and Minella Study look best placed with their proven Grade-level form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner dominance
scenarios.trigger: If either Lord or Aqua Bleu gets an uncontested lead and dictates fractions
scenarios.body: The leader can control the race and kick clear before the prominent runners can respond on testing ground. Lord's course form and Aqua Bleu's willing attitude make them dangerous if unopposed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or traffic problems eliminate most of the field
scenarios.body: Indian River or Wolf Rayet can benefit from a slowly-run race or when others encounter trouble in the congested pack. The soft ground aids their late-running style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapse scramble
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders tire dramatically and the prominent runners also struggle
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where any horse still travelling can win, potentially opening the door for an outsider. Ammes could benefit despite his recent absence.

watchPoints.text: Lord and Aqua Bleu's early duel intensity will determine if they survive or set up the race for closers
Traffic problems likely for Mange Tout, Selma De Vary, Winston Junior and Maestro Conti in the prominent pack from 3 out
Indian River and Wolf Rayet need significant pace pressure or traffic issues to get competitive from hold-up positions
Maestro Conti's market support reflects strong stable form with Harry Skelton's 10/44 recent record
Minella Study's Triumph run suggests he belongs at this level despite relatively inexperienced connections

races.name: William Hill Manifesto Novices' Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lulamba
runners_data.note: Natural leader with proven class but Arkle mistake suggests jumping remains a slight concern despite excellent overall record
runners_data.comment: Beaten favourite in the Arkle; has otherwise been a rising star; this new trip should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; ran creditably on the figures but was only third when favourite for the Arkle, in which a mistake two out cost him some ground when challenging; has otherwise been a rising force at about 2m and his record away from the Cheltenham Festival is 6-6, comfortably beating his elders in the Game Spirit for the most recent success; gives the firm impression he's ready for a crack at this new trip; sets the standard and retains the potential for rating higher still.

runners_data.name: Blueking d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who benefits from cheekpieces fitted and Paul Nicholls' strong 27% strike-rate with Harry Cobden
runners_data.comment: Won a substandard Rising Stars; close second in handicap last time; this is a stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: Useful 2m4f novice chaser but he won a substandard edition of the Rising Stars at Wincanton and his close second at Kempton (with cheekpieces fitted) last time was achieved in a handicap; faces a stiffer task at this level in the retained headgear.

runners_data.name: Koktail Divin
runners_data.note: Proven non-stayer over 3m+ so this drop back to 2m4f should suit his prominent style perfectly
runners_data.comment: Non-stayer in the 3m1f Brown Advisory; broadly progressive otherwise; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Non-stayer (shaped better than the bare result) in the 3m1f Brown Advisory at Cheltenham having surprisingly swerved the 2m4f Jack Richards option; broadly progressive otherwise and scored by a wide margin at Leopardstown (2m5f, yielding) the time before, recording a very useful RPR; ran well in the Mersey over hurdles at this meeting 12 months ago; remains of major interest, back down in distance.

runners_data.name: Jax Junior
runners_data.note: Front-runner who was well beaten by Lulamba last time but the step up in trip should help his stamina-laden style
runners_data.comment: Has a good strike-rate when racing beyond 2m, the most recent success in Kempton Grade 2
runners_data.spotlight: Finished 18l behind Lulamba in the Arkle but may fare better in this rematch, with the return to further a likely plus; readily bagged Grade 2 honours at Kempton (2m4f, good to soft) the time before, enhancing his good strike-rate when racing beyond 2m.

runners_data.name: Mambonumberfive
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning fresh after 61 days off but faces tactical disadvantage in small field with two confirmed pace-setters
runners_data.comment: Best to forgive latest effort; 3-3 over fences otherwise; may resume improvement; new trip
runners_data.spotlight: Comes here fresh having bypassed the Cheltenham Festival and been absent since a Kingmaker defeat that is perhaps best forgiven due to the heavy ground; 3-3 over fences otherwise, including 2m wins at Aintree (handicap) and Kempton (Grade 2, readily); may resume improvement, provided he stays the new trip.

races.paceDynamic: Lulamba and Jax Junior will set a genuine gallop from the start, with both proven front-runners likely to contest the early lead over this stamina-testing 2m4f trip. The small field of five means little shelter for the hold-up horses, with the pace likely to be honest throughout rather than stop-start. Blueking d'Oroux and Koktail Divin will track the leaders prominently, while Mambonumberfive faces the toughest task from his hold-up style. This honest pace scenario strongly favours the prominent racers who can track the leaders without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Lulamba and Jax Junior maintain a strong pace without one capitulating early
scenarios.body: The honest gallop plays to stamina strengths over this extended trip, allowing the classier horses to assert late. Prominent trackers get first run on tiring leaders while avoiding early speed battles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Speed Duel Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If Lulamba and Jax Junior go too fast early and both weaken significantly
scenarios.body: The fierce early pace sets up the race for horses held up or tracking at a safe distance. The small field means less cover but also less interference for late runners to navigate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If either Lulamba or Jax Junior gets an uncontested lead and maintains rhythm
scenarios.body: One leader gets away with controlled fractions while the other front-runner either doesn't fire or gets restrained. The winner maintains momentum while others struggle to make up ground late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners are unusually restrained creating a slow early pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish which doesn't suit the distance specialists in this field. The tactical nature creates traffic problems and favours the handiest horses with most natural speed.

watchPoints.text: Lulamba's jumping under pressure - made crucial mistake two out in Arkle when challenging and any repeat could be costly
Jax Junior's early tactics - if he tries to match Lulamba's pace from the start he may pay late over this trip
Mambonumberfive's ring-rustiness - 61 days off is significant and he needs the race to develop perfectly from his hold-up style
Blueking d'Oroux with cheekpieces on for first time since his improved Kempton second - headgear change could spark improvement
Going conditions remaining consistent - any further softening would particularly impact Koktail Divin who has shown less form on heavy

races.name: Racing Welfare Bowl Chase (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pic d'Orhy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with Harry Cobden aboard returns after 54 days off but showed excellent form when second to Jonbon at Ascot in February
runners_data.comment: 11yo; three Grade 1 wins (including here); looked as good as ever last time; not ruled out
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who looked as good as ever when runner-up in a captivating battle with Jonbon in the Ascot Chase (2m5f, good to soft) in February, when bidding to win that Grade 1 for the third consecutive year; won the Grade 1 Melling Chase here (2m4f, soft) in 2023; seemed fine at 3m when 1l second in this season's Charlie Hall (good) and his trainer has won this race six times; no surprise to see a bold bid from this front-runner, who is not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Impaire Et Passe
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Townend/Mullins who was pulled up at Cheltenham but has won at this meeting in consecutive years previously
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in the Ryanair but 2-2 at this meeting and could bounce back with a big run
runners_data.spotlight: Unproven at this trip and reportedly never travelling when pulled up in the Ryanair at Cheltenham last month; however, he's won at this meeting in each of the last two seasons, landing the Grade 1 Manifesto Novices' Chase last April (2m4f, good to soft; Jango Baie third), and he produced a top performance in the Grade 2 Red Mills Chase at Gowran Park this February; could bounce back with big run for last year's winning trainer Willie Mullins.

runners_data.name: Jango Baie
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has improved markedly for longer trips this season and finished close fourth in the King George at Kempton
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in the Gold Cup; leading claims if that hard race 27 days ago hasn't left a mark
runners_data.spotlight: Kept on for close third to Impaire Et Passe in the 2m4f Manifesto here 12 months ago and has improved for longer trips this season; very close fourth in thrilling finish to the King George at Kempton (3m, good) in December and 8l second in the Gold Cup at Cheltenham (3m2f, good to soft) last month; leading claims if that hard race 27 days ago hasn't left a mark.

runners_data.name: Spillane's Tower
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 75 days off following Grade 2 Cotswold Chase victory but unproven trainer Mangan has poor strike-rate
runners_data.comment: Won Grade 2 Cotswold Chase; others have achieved more but he's open to further improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won two Grade 1s in Ireland in spring 2024 during novice chase campaign (2m4f/3m1f, heavy/yielding) and posted first win since in the Grade 2 Cotswold Chase at Cheltenham (3m1f, soft) this January; he was receiving 6lb from close runner-up L'Homme Presse last time and others in this have achieved more, but he's only eight and could still have improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Protektorat
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old prominent runner who kept on well for second to Jonbon in the Melling Chase here last year over shorter trip
runners_data.comment: 11yo; no Grade 1 win since March 2024 but still capable of strong form; possible contender
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo whose last Grade 1 win came in March 2024 but he showed strong form when keeping on for second of four to Jonbon in the Melling Chase here (2m4f, good) 12 months ago and has won at Windsor (2m6f, soft; warm conditions race) and Kelso (extended 2m7f, good to soft; Listed) on his two runs this year; he should still be fine at this sort of trip and could be a contender.

races.paceDynamic: Pic d'Orhy will lead from the start with his confirmed front-running style, likely setting a sustainable gallop over this extended trip without early pressure from the small field. Jango Baie and Protektorat will track in prominent positions behind the leader, while hold-up horses Impaire Et Passe and Spillane's Tower will settle towards the rear. The lack of pace pressure should create a tactical finish where positioning and stamina become crucial over the final half-mile. This honest gallop strongly favours the prominent racers and front-runner who can control the tempo and have first run on the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Pic d'Orhy sets an uncontested lead and maintains his jumping rhythm.
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old can dictate terms without pressure and kick clear approaching the final fence, making it difficult for closers to peg him back. His recent Ascot Chase form with Jonbon confirms he retains his best form at this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Jango Baie or Protektorat sit perfectly in Pic d'Orhy's slipstream and time their challenge.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners can stalk the leader's honest pace before delivering a telling blow in the final furlong when the front-runner begins to tire. Their tactical positioning gives them every chance to strike gold.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes slower than expected and the hold-up horses get an ideal setup.
scenarios.body: Spillane's Tower and Impaire Et Passe can capitalize on a dawdling gallop with their strong finishing kicks from off the pace. The lack of early speed allows them to close dramatically in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Drama
scenarios.trigger: If Pic d'Orhy jumps poorly or fades dramatically after setting the pace.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble in the final half-mile with no clear leader, allowing any horse with energy reserves to capitalize on the chaos. This unpredictable finish opens the door for any runner to strike.

watchPoints.text: Impaire Et Passe traveled poorly when pulled up at Cheltenham last month and needs to bounce back to form immediately
Spillane's Tower faces a significant step up in class under an inexperienced trainer with just one runner in the last 14 days
Pic d'Orhy's jumping rhythm in the early stages will determine if he can control this race from the front as expected
The lack of early pace pressure could set up perfectly for the two hold-up horses if the gallop becomes pedestrian
Jango Baie's positioning behind Pic d'Orhy will be crucial for Nico de Boinville to time his challenge effectively

races.name: Randox Foxhunters' Open Hunters' Chase

runners_data.name: Gaboriot
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with poor recent form and concerning pull-up record over these fences
runners_data.comment: Return to form needed but twice placed over these fences and gets a change of headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in Becher here in December and his two subsequent hunter chase runs have yielded an early fall and disappointing defeat; twice placed over these fences, however, most recently in the Grand Sefton over C&D in November, and could have an each-way shout if back on song in a change of headgear.

runners_data.name: Thunder Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with proven class but questionable stamina at this trip for 10-year-old legs
runners_data.comment: Very talented in his prime; easy hunter chase wins on last two starts; could be in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: Very talented in his prime; this 10yo isn't the force of old and today's race is much tougher than the hunter chases he's won easily on his last two starts (2m4f, good to soft/good), but if he can tap further into his back-class he may well be in the mix; James King has won this twice.

runners_data.name: Its On The Line
runners_data.note: Prominent racer, defending champion with excellent record on similar going and strong Cheltenham form
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2024; went close again at Cheltenham last month and he's entitled to respect
runners_data.spotlight: Won this in 2024 (heavy); beaten a neck by Barton Snow at last month's Cheltenham Festival (3m2f, good to soft), finishing a close second in that hunter chase for the third season in a row; at this trip he may prefer more testing ground than is likely today, but he's still entitled to respect.

runners_data.name: Java Point
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but first-time headgear suggests connections have concerns about focus
runners_data.comment: 11yo who has been in good form since tackling hunter chases but needs a bigger run today
runners_data.spotlight: Useful, four-time handicap chase winner who scored at Ludlow (3m, good to soft) in January on his first handicap chase start; runner-up on next two outings (3m/2m7f, soft/good to soft); this 11yo needs a bigger run today.

runners_data.name: Willewonga
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with alarming recent pull-up record including 100-1 failure at Cheltenham
runners_data.comment: Pulled up at Cheltenham last month but after a break; might not be a forlorn hope each-way
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up at 50-1 in this last year and same outcome at the Cheltenham Festival last month, when 100-1; however, that latest outing was his first run for 110 days and he may have needed it; in front when making a bad blunder at the final fence at Bangor (3m, soft) last February and that form suggests he might not be a forlorn hope each-way, at what should be a big price.

runners_data.name: Take All
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form behind Java Point, topspeed figure suggests finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Ran well for a long way at Cheltenham; could have an each-way shout now back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Good efforts in defeat behind Java Point (3m, good to soft) and Unexposed Party (2m6f, good to soft) this year and ran well for a long way before fading at last month's Cheltenham Festival (3m2f, good to soft); could have an each-way shout at big odds now back down in trip; cheekpieces replace hood.

runners_data.name: Joker De Mai
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 48-day break after early fall in this race last year
runners_data.comment: Caught the eye two starts ago but he has to step up on this season's handicap form
runners_data.spotlight: 7-1 when an early faller at the Chair in this race 12 months ago; this 7yo was an eyecatching third at Ludlow in February, having been hampered, but he needs to step up on this season's handicap form if he's to threaten.

runners_data.name: Lets Go Champ
runners_data.note: Prominent mare with useful recent form but switching trainers adds slight question mark
runners_data.comment: Beat a very solid yardstick for last month's hunter chase win and firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Won a competitive handicap chase at the Punchestown festival in May 2024 for Henry de Bromhead (2m4f, good to yielding) and he showed when winning a hunter chase at Gowran Park (3m1f, heavy) last month that he retains considerable ability at the age of 11; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Gracchus De Balme
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won this race last year but pulled up badly at Cheltenham latest
runners_data.comment: Pulled up at Cheltenham Festival but won this last year and he's capable of bouncing back
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up at the Cheltenham Festival (3m2f, good to soft) last month; however, he was pulled up at Leicester last February prior to winning this race at 22-1 (good to soft), so he's capable of bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Empire De Maulde
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying first-time headgear at age 12, needs career-best effort
runners_data.comment: Four point wins last year but this 12yo hasn't shone in 2026
runners_data.spotlight: Four point wins last year and runner-up in two hunter chases last spring (2m7f/2m6f, good to soft/good); however, he'll need to improve upon that form and this 12yo hasn't shone on either outing this year.

runners_data.name: Enqarde
runners_data.note: Hold-up 12-year-old with first-time headgear who pulled up badly at Exeter after Leicester win
runners_data.comment: 50-1 winner at Leicester in February but pulled up at Exeter since; probably vulnerable
runners_data.spotlight: Career highlight was the Tommy Whittle at Haydock in 2021; 50-1 winner of four-runner hunter chase at Leicester (2m6f, soft) this February but pulled up at Exeter (3m, good to soft) since; this 12yo is probably vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Fan De Blues
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 43-day break with first-time headgear for new trainer
runners_data.comment: Very useful in his prime; not devoid of promise for this yard but needs a step forward
runners_data.spotlight: Very useful for Willie Mullins and ran pretty well over these fences in the 2023 Topham; following a long absence this 11yo hasn't been devoid of promise for his new yard, but needs to take a significant step forward.

runners_data.name: Music Drive
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid Cheltenham Festival form who handles these fences well
runners_data.comment: Again made the frame at 33-1 in the Cheltenham Festival hunter chase; each-way contender
runners_data.spotlight: He's made the frame at 33-1 in the last two runnings of the Cheltenham Festival hunter chase, finishing about 8l behind Barton Snow and Its On The Line last month when third; tackles a new track today and the drop back in trip isn't an obvious positive, but he could still be an each-way contender.

runners_data.name: Golden Son
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with easy hunter chase wins this year but disappointing Cheltenham effort
runners_data.comment: 14l fourth at Cheltenham last month; work to do but the drop back in trip may help
runners_data.spotlight: Useful handicapper who posted easy wins this year in his first two hunter chases (3m/2m7f, good to soft/heavy); 14l fourth at the Cheltenham Festival last month (3m2f, good to soft) so has work to do with some of these, but he was left behind up the hill and is not ruled out now back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Unexpected Party
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong credentials returning from 54-day break for champion trainer
runners_data.comment: Comfortable wins over 2m5f/2m6f on last two starts; holds leading form claims
runners_data.spotlight: Won the Grand Annual (2m, soft) in March 2024 and runner-up in same race last year (2m, good to soft); comfortable wins in hunter chases on last two starts (2m5f/2m6f, good/good to soft); his stamina will be more severely tested in today's hotter company but leading claims if seeing it out.

runners_data.name: Barton Snow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with perfect 5-5 record under rules including narrow Cheltenham Festival victory
runners_data.comment: Won the big one at Cheltenham last month & should be fine back down in trip; major player
runners_data.spotlight: Proved his stamina and made it 5-5 under rules (all in hunter chases) when beating Its On The Line by a neck to win the big one at Cheltenham (3m2f, good to soft) last month, despite a mistake at the final fence; has also won on good going; he doesn't appear to be straightforward but clearly knows how to win and should be fine now back down in trip; major player.

runners_data.name: A Moments Madness
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader making stable debut, progressive form but significant class step-up required
runners_data.comment: His comeback third at Carlisle can be upgraded; could go well at sizeable odds
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in handicap chases last spring for Warren Greatrex (2m2f/2m3f, good/soft) and last month's third on stable debut in a hunter chase at Carlisle (2m5f, good to soft), after an absence, can be upgraded as he hung left at that right-handed track; has plenty to find but this 7yo is very lightly raced and, now going left-handed, could go well at sizeable odds.

runners_data.name: Snipe
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good recent hunter chase form including course-and-distance success
runners_data.comment: 2-3 in hunter chases but he needs a clear career-best if he's to win this
runners_data.spotlight: Won on his first hunter chase start at Hereford (2m5f, soft) in January and bounced back from heavy defeat behind Golden Son at Taunton (2m7f, heavy) to win at Leicester (2m, good to soft) last month; however, he needs a clear career-best if he's to win this.

runners_data.name: Great Notions
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with consistent recent efforts but needs significant improvement in class
runners_data.comment: Some good runs in defeat in handicaps since November but plenty to find today
runners_data.spotlight: Won maiden hunter chase at Hexham (3m, good) last May; some good runs in defeat in handicaps since November, most recently 5l second at Sedgefield (3m2f, good), but he has plenty to find today.

runners_data.name: Famous Clermont
runners_data.note: Prominent runner and former winner returning from 314-day absence with point-to-point prep
runners_data.comment: Won this in 2023 but this 11yo probably isn't as good as he once was; others are preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Won this in 2023 (good to soft) and bagged further hunter chase wins in the same Stratford race in May 2024/2025 (2m6f, good); won a point last month and he's better than he showed when tailed off in this last April, but this 11yo probably isn't as good as he once was and others are preferred.

runners_data.name: Fairly Famous
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with strong hunter chase record but also returning from 314-day break
runners_data.comment: In good heart in points but last May's hunter chase form suggests he's up against it
runners_data.spotlight: Strong form when winning hunter chases at Cheltenham in May 2023 and May 2024; in good heart in point-to-points this season but last May's hunter chase form suggests he may be found wanting this afternoon.

runners_data.name: A Jet Of Our Own
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finished creditable fifth at 125-1 in this race last year
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy on this year's form but ran well when fifth of 29 at 125-1 in this last term
runners_data.spotlight: Very hard to fancy judged on this year's hunter chase form but he took a big step forward when fifth of 29 at 125-1 in this race last April (good to soft), and is not ruled out each-way now back over these obstacles.

runners_data.name: Densworth
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose form has deteriorated badly since promising 2024 Wetherby success
runners_data.comment: The odd snippet of useful form in 2024 but down the pecking order on subsequent evidence
runners_data.spotlight: Showed the odd snippet of very useful form in 2024, winning easily at Wetherby (2m3f, good) that November on his second chase start; however, his subsequent exploits put him well down the pecking order in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Hollywood Harmon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying 7lb penalty but well beaten in recent Carlisle hunter chase
runners_data.comment: Won maiden hunter chase at Cartmel last May but she would be a shock winner today
runners_data.spotlight: Easily won a maiden hunter chase at Cartmel (2m5f, good to soft) last May; didn't run badly at Fakenham (3m, soft) in February but well beaten at Carlisle (2m5f, good to soft) since and she would be a shock winner.

runners_data.name: Whats The Solution
runners_data.note: Prominent point-to-point specialist making rare hunter chase appearance after 314-day break
runners_data.comment: Ran okay last May in sole previous hunter chase but looks up against it today
runners_data.spotlight: 5-17 in points, his latest win in that sphere coming last month; 12l third of six to Barton Snow at Stratford (2m6f, good) last May in his sole previous hunter chase and he looks up against it today.

races.paceDynamic: A Moments Madness will lead from the start at a steady gallop, but won't face genuine early pressure with most rivals wanting prominent positions rather than disputing the lead. The real battle develops from 3f out when the 10+ prominent runners including Its On The Line, Barton Snow, Golden Son, and Unexpected Party start jostling for position on the run to the penultimate fence - creating significant traffic problems. Hold-up horses like Thunder Rock and Take All get cleaner runs but face a stamina test over this trip on testing ground. This pace profile strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good early positions and avoid the mid-race congestion.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Brigade Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses avoid traffic and A Moments Madness sets reasonable fractions
scenarios.body: The class horses who travel prominently get first run while hold-up horses struggle to make ground through tired legs on soft ground. Barton Snow and Its On The Line have the perfect combination of class and tactical speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Strike
scenarios.trigger: If A Moments Madness goes too fast or the prominent pack go at unsustainable pace early
scenarios.body: The pace collapses from 3f out allowing the hold-up horses to sweep through tired leaders. Thunder Rock's class and Take All's strong finishing kick become major assets when others stop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If several prominent runners fall or make mistakes at key fences creating gaps
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with mid-division horses suddenly finding themselves in contention. Music Drive and Fan De Blues can capitalize on their experience over these fences.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wire-to-Wire Shock
scenarios.trigger: If A Moments Madness maintains strong gallop and prominent pack fails to organize pursuit
scenarios.body: The leader's sustainable pace and lack of early pressure allows him to build an unassailable lead. Class horses get caught flat-footed by the lack of genuine pace pressure.

watchPoints.text: Traffic chaos developing from 3f out when 10+ prominent runners including Its On The Line, Golden Son, and Unexpected Party converge
A Moments Madness maintaining strong gallop could catch prominent pack napping if they fail to organize early pursuit
Thunder Rock and Barton Snow getting clear runs through hold-up tactics while prominent horses clash
Multiple horses returning from 300+ day breaks including Famous Clermont and Fairly Famous lacking recent match fitness
First-time headgear on Java Point, Empire De Maulde, Enqarde, and Fan De Blues suggesting trainer concerns

races.name: William Hill Aintree Hurdle (Grade 1) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: El Fabiolo
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning to hurdles after chase jumping issues, 38 days off could leave him vulnerable late despite his class
runners_data.comment: Latest win took hurdles record to 4-7; the best horse in this if viewed on peak chase form
runners_data.spotlight: Probably acts on any going; high class over fences until jumping issues developed; has proved suited by the return to hurdles and an easy win at Leopardstown (2m2f) last time took his record in this sphere to 4-7; the best horse in this field if viewed on his peak chase form.

runners_data.name: The New Lion
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with highest TopSpeed rating who shaped like this trip would suit in the Champion Hurdle
runners_data.comment: Ran well in the Champion Hurdle; leading novice at about 2m4f last term; commands respect
runners_data.spotlight: Broadly progressive; has gone down the Champion Hurdle route this season and ran well in that race most recently, while leaving the impression he's ready for a return to further than 2m; leading novice hurdler at about 2m4f last term, winning the Challow and the Turners (both on good to soft ground); still unbeaten over this sort of distance and commands respect.

runners_data.name: Lucky Place
runners_data.note: Prominent style but disappointing Festival effort raises questions about current form level
runners_data.comment: Still needs to prove he's a Grade 1 hurdler and has the worst chance at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Went for a handicap option at the latest Cheltenham Festival and was well beaten, albeit with the race not panning out totally smoothly; dual Grade 2 winner last term but still needs to prove he's a Grade 1 hurdler and has the worst chance at the weights in this field.

runners_data.name: Alexei
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner who acts on any ground and showed Champion Hurdle form this season
runners_data.comment: Good strike-rate; ran well in the Champion Hurdle and remains a progressive sort
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; good strike-rate includes wins in the Greatwood and Kingwell this season; ties in with Brighterdaysahead and The New Lion on Champion Hurdle running where a late blunder cost him ground when challenging for the places; has form at up to 2m3f; remains a progressive sort.

runners_data.name: Golden Ace
runners_data.note: Fortunate Champion Hurdle winner carrying 7lbs less, prominent style suits but needs to find more
runners_data.comment: Registered her Grade 1 wins in fortuitous fashion and is going to need further luck
runners_data.spotlight: Fortuitous winner of the 2025 Champion Hurdle (same story in the Fighting Fifth) and finished only fifth, behind some of today's rivals, when attempting to retain her crown; largely consistent and has won over 2m4f but increasing her Grade 1 tally may require further luck.

runners_data.name: Brighterdaysahead
runners_data.note: High-class prominent runner with excellent TopSpeed figure who may prefer this trip to two miles
runners_data.comment: Very smart mare; easy winner at this meeting in 2024; has leading claims at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Has form on most types of ground; took her Cheltenham Festival record to 0-3 with a defeat in the latest Champion Hurdle but that was a respectable effort without managing to confirm placings with Lossiemouth, who had played second fiddle in the Irish equivalent; record of 2-3 at about 2m4f includes an easy success in the Mersey at this meeting two years ago; very smart mare who holds leading claims at the weights.

runners_data.name: Potters Charm
runners_data.note: Freshest runner having missed Cheltenham, prominent style and 46-day break could be tactical advantage
runners_data.comment: Record of 7-11 over hurdles; 1-1 at Aintree (Gr 1 novice) and he's the freshest contender
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; the freshest contender in this race, having bypassed the Cheltenham Festival and been absent since landing the National Spirit at Fontwell (2m3f) over six weeks ago when taking hurdles record to 7-11; sole attempt at Aintree resulted in a Grade 1 novice success on Boxing Day 2024; likely to go well.

races.paceDynamic: El Fabiolo will lead uncontested from the start with his natural front-running style, setting a sustainable gallop that won't stretch the field early. The remaining six runners all show prominent tendencies, meaning they'll track El Fabiolo in a compact group rather than applying early pressure. This creates a tactical race where positioning into the straight becomes crucial, with the pace likely to quicken significantly from the final flight. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners with proven finishing kicks, particularly those who can quicken best off a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Kick Decides
scenarios.trigger: If El Fabiolo sets a steady pace and the field stays bunched turning in
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last flight where class and finishing speed decide the outcome. The New Lion and Brighterdaysahead have the highest TopSpeed ratings and proven ability to quicken decisively.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If El Fabiolo finds his jumping rhythm and the pace quickens earlier than expected
scenarios.body: Paul Townend utilizes El Fabiolo's class to stretch the field approaching two out, making it hard for closers to reel him in. His recent Leopardstown win showed he retains his old brilliance when everything clicks.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground and 2m4f trip catch out the milers when the pace lifts
scenarios.body: The longer distance starts to tell in the final furlong, favouring those with proven stamina reserves. Potters Charm's freshness and Alexei's versatility over trips become decisive factors late on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Suits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems or jumping errors disrupt the rhythm of the market leaders
scenarios.body: The race falls apart tactically, allowing a patient ride on an outsider to pick up the pieces. Lucky Place or Golden Ace could benefit from chaos ahead given their lower weight expectations.

watchPoints.text: El Fabiolo's jumping under pressure - any mistakes could end his chance quickly given his recent chasing problems
The New Lion's position turning in - needs to be handy to utilize his superior finishing speed effectively
Brighterdaysahead's stamina reserves - TopSpeed suggests she has gears but 2m4f still relatively unexplored
Potters Charm's freshness advantage - 46 days off could provide extra zip in the finish that others lack
Golden Ace's weight advantage - 7lbs less than main rivals could prove significant in a tight finish

races.name: Close Brothers Red Rum Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Inthepocket
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with mixed fence record, fell when going well at Cheltenham, first-time headgear could help focus
runners_data.comment: Made headway in the Grand Annual prior to falling two out; his finest hour came here
runners_data.spotlight: His fortunes over fences have been mixed but he made good headway in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good) last month prior to falling two out; finest hour came when winning Grade 1 Top Novices' Hurdle here (2m, good to soft) in April 2023; could have a big say if avoiding mishap.

runners_data.name: Hercule Du Seuil
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer who won Grade 3 for Mullins, below par recently but drops to handy mark
runners_data.comment: Ex-Willie Mullins; won Grade 3 chase last May but hard to fancy on more recent evidence
runners_data.spotlight: Won Grade 3 at Killarney (2m4f, yielding) last May for Willie Mullins and he's on a handy mark on that form; however, below par in the winter on final two starts for that yard and soundly beaten in handicaps on both outings for this stable; usual hood is left off; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Boothill
runners_data.note: Ascot specialist making Aintree debut, hold-up style suits moderate pace, wind surgery addressed breathing issues
runners_data.comment: 8th in the Grand Annual and 4lb lower today, but this 11yo needs to find something extra
runners_data.spotlight: Ascot specialist who runs at Aintree for the first time; following wind surgery he ran okay when 13l eighth of 20 in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good) last month, and he's another 4lb lower today; however, this 11yo is without a win since 2023 and needs to find something extra now in cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Javert Allen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who ran well at this course and distance, long absence since February could blunt fitness edge
runners_data.comment: Below par last time but in good form otherwise this season and could make a bold bid
runners_data.spotlight: Below par at Kempton (2m4f) in February last time but he's run well in defeat otherwise this season, including when fourth over C&D (good to soft) on his reappearance in a race that worked out extremely well; this front-runner could make a bold bid in first-time cheekpieces back at 2m.

runners_data.name: Grain d'Oudairies
runners_data.note: Progressive ten-year-old with prominent style, fresh after 52-day break but may need the run
runners_data.comment: 10yo who has enjoyed a progressive season but this may prove too competitive
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who hasn't had much racing for his age and has been progressive this term, with wins at Kelso (2m1f, good to soft) and Haydock (2m4f, good to soft); however, below par at Carlisle in February last time and, even if back on song, there's a firm suspicion this will prove too competitive.

runners_data.name: Sans Bruit
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter with excellent April record, 81 days off but won this race twice previously in this month
runners_data.comment: Has won last two runnings of this race; did it comfortably last year when just 3lb lower
runners_data.spotlight: His exploits earlier in the season aren't of much concern given his last five wins have come in the month of April, including the last two runnings of this race (soft/good to soft; has also won on good); this prominent racer did it comfortably 12 months ago and is just 3lb higher today; could once more take all the beating.

runners_data.name: Stencil
runners_data.note: French-trained hold-up performer who impressed at Chepstow, needs to bounce back from disappointing Cheltenham effort
runners_data.comment: 5yo who ran better than the bare facts at Cheltenham; interesting now back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: 5yo; trained in France but campaigned in Britain since start of 2025; impressed in a warm novice chase at Chepstow (2m, soft) in January and 25l tenth in the Jack Richards at Cheltenham (2m4f, good) was better than the bare facts, as he pulled hard and was held up in a race that favoured those who were up with the pace; could settle better now back down in trip; interesting.

runners_data.name: Highlands Legacy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good course form, 81-day absence since Windsor win could affect sharpness
runners_data.comment: Enjoying a progressive first campaign over fences; every chance he'll continue to improve
runners_data.spotlight: Won on chase debut at Worcester (2m, good) in October and runner-up on next two starts (including C&D) before narrow win at Windsor (2m, soft) in January; he's 6lb higher than last time and in a hotter race today, but this progressive 7yo may be able to find the necessary further improvement.

runners_data.name: Jasko Des Dames
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who led at Cheltenham before fading, returned to form on better ground last time
runners_data.comment: Led jumping 2 out in the Grand Annual (when 5th); this less demanding track could be ideal
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form back on better ground when fifth, beaten just over 10l, in the Grand Annual at Cheltenham (2m, good); he led jumping two out at the Festival and this less demanding track could be right up his street.

runners_data.name: Dr T J Eckleburg
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse racing off 10lb lower mark than when fifth in this last year, consistent without winning
runners_data.comment: 10lb lower than when fifth in this last year but others arrive with more pressing claims
runners_data.spotlight: Runs off a mark 10lb lower than when fifth of 14 in this last year, beaten just over 13l; he's run a couple of reasonable races this season but hasn't shown enough to suggest he's the one to be on today.

runners_data.name: Ryan's Rocket
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer dropping back in trip, won at Newbury over shorter when last seen at his best
runners_data.comment: Firmly in the picture on his November win but his jumping might be put under pressure here
runners_data.spotlight: Firmly in the picture judged on his handicap win at Newbury (2m, good to soft) in November and he drops back in trip today having weakened over 2m4f at Kempton last month; not ruled out but he made mistakes last time and has unseated on two of his last four starts; needs to cut out the blunders.

runners_data.name: Brookie
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose form has collapsed, pulled up last two starts including Champion Chase debacle
runners_data.comment: Hard to say what sort of form he's in but this C&D brought out very best in him last April
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in Ascot handicap in November and tailed off on sole outing since in the Champion Chase last month; it's hard to say what sort of form he's in but this C&D brought out the very best in him when runner-up in the Grade 1 Maghull Novices' Chase (good) 12 months ago; could go well back here.

runners_data.name: Wonleg
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 104-day break, won at Wexford but needs career-best performance here
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 6yo who represents a top Irish trainer and may yet have more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Won Wexford handicap (2m, good) last July on third chase start and returned to form when third of 20 at Leopardstown (2m1f, yielding) in December; needs a career best today but this unexposed 6yo represents a top Irish trainer (who saddles three) and could yet have more to offer.

runners_data.name: Petit Tonnerre
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was tailed off recently, won big handicap previously but form has deserted him
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on his last three starts but not discounted in view of last May's Irish win
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten ninth in this 12 months ago (good to soft) and tailed off on his last three starts; however, the return to better ground can help and he won a big-field handicap at Punchestown (2m, yielding) last May; on a handy mark judged on that Irish form and he's not discounted.

runners_data.name: Palamon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won convincingly at Bangor nine days ago, reapplied tongue-tie and return to good ground helped
runners_data.comment: Well backed when returning to form with ready win at Bangor; not ruled out off 9lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Well-backed, even-money favourite at Bangor (2m4f) last Tuesday, when reverting to good ground in a reapplied tongue-tie and returning to form with a convincing win; 9lb higher in a much hotter race today but not ruled out for his top yard on the back of that stylish success.

races.paceDynamic: Sans Bruit will take the field along at a steady gallop from the front, with no obvious pressure from the sparse pace presence. Javert Allen, Grain d'Oudairies, Jasko Des Dames, and Wonleg may track him in the early stages, but none are confirmed pace forcers. The sustainable tempo will keep the field bunched turning for home, allowing hold-up horses time to organize their challenges. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses and strong finishers who can produce late kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Sans Bruit maintains an uncontested lead into the straight
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows closers like Hercule Du Seuil, Stencil, and Highlands Legacy to get organized and unleash finishing kicks. Late runners benefit from the strong gallop and get first run on the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can get first run on Sans Bruit
scenarios.body: Javert Allen or Grain d'Oudairies could capitalize on tracking the pace and having position when the race develops. They get the jump on the hold-up brigade who may be caught flat-footed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sans Bruit Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even more sedate than expected and no one challenges early
scenarios.body: The front-runner gets an armchair ride and kicks clear before the closers can respond. His stamina for the minimum trip becomes an asset rather than a liability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Sans Bruit stops quickly and the race becomes a sprint from the last
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery where any horse with a bit of zip can grab it. Fitness and recent form become more important than running style.

watchPoints.text: Sans Bruit could get an uncontested lead and prove very hard to peg back if allowed his own way in front
Hercule Du Seuil drops significantly in class from his winter campaign and could be overpriced given his ability
Stencil bounced back to form dramatically at Chepstow and could repeat that improvement on suitable ground
Multiple Henry De Bromhead runners (Inthepocket, Jasko Des Dames, Wonleg) could work tactically together in race
Palamon's impressive Bangor win just nine days ago suggests he's hit form at the right time with quick turnaround

races.name: Goffs Nickel Coin Mares' Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (Grade 2) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Divine Diva
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant returning from 145-day break faces tough ask against this strong pace
runners_data.comment: Needs to show progress; Harry Skelton duly prefers new stablemate Nan's Choice
runners_data.spotlight: Got the better of Lennon Grove in Irish point then bagged a bronze medal in Listed grade at Cheltenham; however, needs to show progress and Harry Skelton duly prefers interesting new stablemate Nan's Choice.

runners_data.name: Fairy Park
runners_data.note: Patient type ideally suited to sit behind the guaranteed pace battle and finish strongly
runners_data.comment: Irish point winner; fared best of the rest behind unbeaten Princess Day at Newbury
runners_data.spotlight: Easily justified favouritism in Irish point then fared best of the rest behind Princess Day at Newbury (good to soft); could go well, albeit seems unlikely to reverse placings with that rival who remains unbeaten.

runners_data.name: Ti'mamzel
runners_data.note: Perfect hold-up profile with excellent soft ground form makes her major player
runners_data.comment: Strong record features two Listed wins, latest in emphatic style at Sandown; major player
runners_data.spotlight: Above-average mare whose strong record (all on soft ground) comprises a good second against males at Windsor flanked by two Listed wins, latest at Sandown where she did it in emphatic fashion; brings major claims to this next step on the ladder.

runners_data.name: It Would Be You
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced hold-up sort stepping up markedly in class but interesting prospect
runners_data.comment: Well on top at Catterick and looks an interesting prospect for Jennie Candlish
runners_data.spotlight: Well on top at the finish in Catterick event (good) and looks an interesting prospect for Jennie Candlish; goes into much deeper waters but could make waves with significant progress possible after one run.

runners_data.name: Martini Majesty
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer from powerful yard but form looks modest for this grade
runners_data.comment: Ascot scorer who should progress and helps to give Alan King an interesting hand
runners_data.spotlight: Related to a very notable Flat stayer for her yard; hard to get excited about the form of her Ascot win (good to soft; beat One Dimensional by 2l) but she should be capable of progress and helps to give Alan King an interesting hand.

runners_data.name: Billey Shiftit
runners_data.note: Brings worst form and wrong running style for this pace setup
runners_data.comment: Brings the worst form having finished only sixth at Wincanton
runners_data.spotlight: Brings the worst form having finished only sixth of 14 in Wincanton contest; may do better in due course but this looks an impossible task.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but form well short of this standard despite yard having second string
runners_data.comment: Won at Hexham then not disgraced at Newcastle; this is much harder
runners_data.spotlight: Far from disgraced at Newcastle when carrying a penalty for her Hexham success; however, looks well short of Graded standard; yard also runs It Would Be You.

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 250-day absence with fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Absent since showing promise with third of 15 at last year's Galway festival
runners_data.spotlight: Absent since showing promise with third of 15, one place behind Midnight Musical, at last year's Galway festival (on good ground); open to improvement but this presents a demanding return to action.

runners_data.name: Burds Of A Feather
runners_data.note: Front-runner with headgear applied, will contribute to fierce early pace
runners_data.comment: Fizzy sort but has potential; wasn't for catching at Warwick on rules debut
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 2-2 in completed starts, namely wide-margin wins on final attempt in Irish points and on rules debut; went freely to post and in the race at Warwick (soft) but wasn't for catching, having soon established a clear lead; withdrawn from Sandown Listed event since, having bolted before the start; has potential provided her fizzy ways can be tamed.

runners_data.name: Tiktok Casey
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter who will help create the speed battle early
runners_data.comment: Rallied to win at Naas on rules debut then ran well in Grade 2 at Leopardstown
runners_data.spotlight: Irish mare who has belied 20-1 and 28-1 odds since switched to rules, rallying to win at Naas (soft to heavy) then good third in Grade 2 Leopardstown event at the Dublin Racing Festival (heavy); seems likely to give supporters a good run for their money.

runners_data.name: Nan's Choice
runners_data.note: Prominent type with Harry Skelton's tactical nous, new to this yard
runners_data.comment: Sold for £115,000 since winning by 5l at Gowran Park; has joined Dan Skelton; interesting
runners_data.spotlight: Has a useful pedigree; won by 5l at Gowran Park (heavy) in the latest of her two outings for Conor Houlihan; sold for £115,000 the following week and has joined Dan Skelton; interesting contender, with any amount of further improvement a possibility.

runners_data.name: Emerald Quest
runners_data.note: Front-runner with tongue-tie fitted, adds to the early speed pressure
runners_data.comment: Had some luck at Huntingdon but breezed clear in the manner of a potentially useful mare
runners_data.spotlight: Avoided trouble and scored easily in an incident-packed race at Huntingdon (soft) with tongue-tie applied on return from lengthy absence; had some luck but breezed clear in a manner that suggests she is potentially useful; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Princess Day
runners_data.note: Unbeaten front-runner with most class but faces pace pressure for first time
runners_data.comment: Won well at Newbury last time; remains unbeaten and has plausible Graded aspirations
runners_data.spotlight: Remains unbeaten, having won her sole attempt in the Irish point-to-point scene and both starts under rules; beat Fairy Park in great style at Newbury (good to soft) most recently, looking a mare who has plausible Graded aspirations; commands respect.

runners_data.name: Ladies Day
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer perfectly placed to benefit from expected pace
runners_data.comment: Point bumper winner who has consistent rules form and ties in with Ti'mamzel
runners_data.spotlight: Point bumper winner whose consistent rules form has culminated in second-place finishes at Aintree (failed only narrowly) and Huntingdon (Listed; behind Ti'mamzel); again likely to give her running.

runners_data.name: One Dimensional
runners_data.note: Hold-up type but lacks the class for this grade elevation
runners_data.comment: Faces a stiff task and is crying out for jumps races over further
runners_data.spotlight: Has consistent RPRs but faces a much stiffer assignment upped in grade and gives the impression, backed up by pedigree, that she's crying out for jumps races over further.

runners_data.name: Roxy Russet
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer who seems outclassed despite recent improvement
runners_data.comment: Ran well behind Seven Stars last time but looks out of her depth at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well behind Seven Stars at Hereford, showing that her fall in the Huntingdon race won by Emerald Quest had left no scars but taking record to 0-3; seems out of her depth at this level.

runners_data.name: Lennon Grove
runners_data.note: Patient type with progressive profile, suits the expected race shape
runners_data.comment: Ran well in the Sandown race won by Ti'mamzel; this Irish mare has progressive RPRs
runners_data.spotlight: Opened her rules account in Thurles event and has since performed well in the Sandown Listed contest (soft) won by Ti'mamzel; this Irish mare brings progressive RPRs, which suggests another good run is likely.

runners_data.name: Seven Stars
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form, major beneficiary of pace setup
runners_data.comment: Likely to build on her Hereford win; related to two mares who were placed in this race
runners_data.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Hereford (good) last time, beating Roxy Russet by 3l and building on a couple of solid efforts; bred to do better still, being related to several winners for her stable, including two mares who were placed in this contest; strong credentials.

runners_data.name: Kiltybo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will help set fierce gallop but may pay late price
runners_data.comment: Has possibilities on the figures but another easy lead is not guaranteed
runners_data.spotlight: Swallowed up in the Thurles race won by Lennon Grove on rules debut but has made all in both starts since and the figure she recorded at Naas (soft to heavy) last time gives her possibilities upped in class; easy lead isn't as certain back in a bigger field, however.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing first-time cheekpieces but poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Has gone the wrong way since finishing second at Galway; headgear applied
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden who has posted a couple of duck eggs since finishing second at the Galway festival on rules debut; first-time headgear needs to have a major effect.

races.paceDynamic: This will be an absolute stamina sapper with Kiltybo, Princess Day, Burds Of A Feather, Tiktok Casey and Emerald Quest all confirmed to go forward early. The quintet of pace-setters will create a relentless gallop from flag to finish, stretching the field and testing stamina reserves to breaking point over 2m1f on testing ground. With such strong early pace guaranteed, this race shape heavily favours the hold-up merchants who can sit and pounce - the prominent racers and front-runners will pay dearly for their early exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Artists Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners engage in their expected pace duel from early
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will set up perfectly for Ti'mamzel, Seven Stars and Ladies Day to storm home late. These patient types can sit off the carnage and use their closing kicks when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Escapes Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Princess Day or Kiltybo can break clear of the other front-runners
scenarios.body: The lone leader could steal enough of a march to hold off the late closers, particularly if they can dictate a steadier middle section. Their class edge becomes decisive when not embroiled in early speed duels.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Nan's Choice or Brave Lady can track the leaders without getting involved in early pace
scenarios.body: These tactical types can position perfectly behind the speed battle then strike when the front-runners falter. Harry Skelton's racecraft on Nan's Choice could prove pivotal in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so fierce that all five front-runners stop dramatically
scenarios.body: Even the hold-up horses struggle to quicken on the testing ground, allowing a mid-division plodder to inherit. This becomes a survival test rather than a speed contest.
